issues.description: The study randomizes and exposes participants in pairs, so the two members of each dyad are not statistically independent. Memory contamination arises through within-pair discussion, making outcomes correlated within pairs. However, the power analysis and planned ANOVA treat 240 individuals as independent observations. This inflates the effective sample size, can underestimate standard errors, and may yield anticonservative p-values. The analysis should account for clustering by pair (e.g., mixed models with pair random effects or pair-level aggregation).
issues.quote: The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs). ... Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups ... The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA

issues.description: The manuscript gives mutually incompatible accounts of when the interventions occur. In the introduction, the warning is first said to be after collaborative recall, later all resistance methods are said to be before collaborative recall, but the actual procedure places them after collaborative recall. This is not a minor wording issue: intervention timing is central to the theoretical rationale (post-warning vs inoculation) and to the interpretation of any effects.
issues.quote: In the present study we decided to place the warning after the collaborative recall (see the rationale for the research below). ... What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation). ... After that, the third phase will take place: it will consist in the procedures to reduce vulnerability to misinformation that were described above.

issues.description: The final memory test is described as open-ended in the procedure, but the analysis plan later states that it will use a two-alternative forced-choice format. These are materially different outcome measures with different scoring, psychometric properties, demand characteristics, and expected effect sizes. This makes the protocol internally inconsistent and undermines the power analysis and planned replication claim.
issues.quote: The test will contain 20 open-ended questions ... Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test ... In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.

issues.description: Discussion status is confounded with specific item identity. The design section claims full counterbalancing of discussed and non-discussed items, but the procedure states that every pair will discuss the same four critical details. If the same items are always discussed, any discussed-vs-non-discussed difference may reflect item difficulty, salience, discriminability, or wording, not misinformation exposure.
issues.quote: In the study, the memory conformity effect will be measured in a within-subjects design and discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced. ... In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase.

issues.description: The manuscript gives two incompatible rules for whether an item counts as containing misinformation. One rule depends on what the partner actually said; the later rule classifies every discussed item as containing misinformation regardless of the actual exchange. This operationalization is invalid because some discussed items may contain no misleading statement, or the partner may even provide the participant's correct version. Misclassifying exposure weakens construct validity and can bias effect estimates.
issues.quote: However, if the partner provided an answer consistent with what the participant had seen, that is, “white mug” (such a situation can happen, e.g., as a result of the partner's guessing), the situation will not be classified as misleading. ... In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation

issues.description: The planned dependent variables are small bounded counts (e.g., number of misinformation-consistent answers out of four or eight items), yet the manuscript proposes ANOVA on aggregate counts. Such data are non-normal, heteroscedastic, and nested within items, participants, and pairs. A binomial/logistic mixed model would be more appropriate. The current plan risks biased standard errors and loss of information.
issues.quote: We will explore the individual memory test’s scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices: the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation, other answers, and the overall number of answers.

issues.description: The analysis plan names numerous outcomes without clearly designating a primary endpoint: four open-ended indices, average accuracy for filler/non-discussed/discussed questions, the omnibus interaction, follow-up group comparisons, and an exploratory DRM predictor. This leaves substantial researcher degrees of freedom in outcome selection and interpretation, increasing false-positive risk and reducing confirmatory value.
issues.quote: We will explore the individual memory test’s scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices: the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation, other answers, and the overall number of answers. Moreover, we will observe the individual memory test’s average accuracy on the filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions.

issues.description: The manuscript anticipates directional significance tests and pairwise follow-ups but does not specify the exact planned contrasts, whether tests are one-tailed, or how multiplicity will be controlled across the many possible comparisons. This creates flexibility in inferential decisions and can inflate Type I error.
issues.quote: Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed. ... In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed.

issues.description: The power analysis is weakly justified. It pools only two prior studies with highly discrepant effect sizes (g = 1.92 vs g = 0.38), assumes a random-effects summary from that tiny base, and treats those studies as using 'the same procedure' even though the current manuscript also describes a modified final test format. The derived pooled effect, conversion to Cohen's f, and repeated-measures correlation are therefore unstable, making the power justification unreliable.
issues.quote: The calculation of the necessary sample size may be based on existing results in which the same procedure as that planned in the proposed study was used ... The existing results as regards effect sizes are Hedges’ g = 1.92, N = 55 (Ito et al., 2019) and Hedges’ g = 0.38, N = 74 (Kękuś et al., 2020). ... with modification concerning applying open-ended questions in the individual memory test.

issues.description: The four conditions are not matched for duration, cognitive load, or engagement. Two conditions are approximately 7-minute passive podcasts, whereas the Demonstration and motivation condition adds an active DRM task, recall worksheet, individualized feedback, and then a podcast. Any group differences could therefore reflect additional delay, arousal, fatigue, effort, or experimenter interaction rather than the intended psychological mechanism.
issues.quote: The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast ... The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast ... First, in order to demonstrate to participants that they are vulnerable to influence, a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used ... Next, the participants’ motivation to resist memory suggestibility will consist in them listening to a podcast

issues.description: The control condition is not matched to the experimental conditions for topic relevance, forensic salience, or expectancy. Experimental groups are explicitly taught about memory errors and misinformation, whereas controls hear about soft skills. Any differences may therefore reflect demand characteristics, perceived study purpose, or motivation to perform carefully, not the proposed mechanisms.
issues.quote: In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.description: The manuscript states that normative influence is 'completely ruled out' because the final test is individual. That is conceptually too strong. Normative pressures can persist after the social interaction, be internalized, or operate through anticipated evaluation, trust, or conflict avoidance. Dismissing this mechanism outright oversimplifies the theory and narrows interpretation without adequate justification.
issues.quote: Given the fact that the individual memory test does not include any element of direct interpersonal pressure, we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study

issues.description: A core theoretical prediction is that the interventions will work better for participants who noticed discrepancies and correctly monitored sources. Yet the protocol does not clearly measure discrepancy awareness or source monitoring as a preregistered variable, so the manuscript cannot actually test this central mechanism or moderator claim.
issues.quote: Thus, we expect that effectiveness of our methods will be higher among people aware of discrepancies between the original information and misinformation than among those unaware of such discrepancies.

issues.description: Open-ended responses must be classified as correct, misinformation-consistent, or other. That requires coding rules and usually multiple coders. The manuscript does not specify how responses will be coded, whether coders will be blind to condition and partner version, or whether inter-rater reliability will be assessed. This omission makes the outcome vulnerable to subjective bias and limits replicability.
issues.quote: The test will contain 20 open-ended questions ... Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers (consistent with the movie), (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers

issues.description: The only explicit exclusion rule concerns technical problems. There is no plan for omitted responses, missing confidence ratings, noncompliance, failed discussions, discovery of the MORI manipulation, or how exclusions will be handled in a dyadic design where one participant's exclusion affects the other participant's exposure. Missing-data handling and pairwise replacement rules are necessary here.
issues.quote: We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.

issues.description: The protocol does not state whether pair members are strangers, friends, or otherwise acquainted, nor whether relationship closeness or trust will be measured. This matters because prior work cited in the references indicates that familiarity and trust can affect memory conformity. Without controlling or recording pair relationship, an important confound remains unaddressed.
issues.quote: The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs). The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet.

issues.description: Critical details appear to include colors and other visual features viewed through polarized glasses and an overlapping dual-projection setup, yet there is no reported screening for color vision deficiencies, visual acuity beyond self-correction, or projector/perceptual calibration checks at the participant level. Misperception of the original stimulus could be mistaken for misinformation effects.
issues.quote: Both versions are identical except for eight critical details: e.g., in the first version, Eric is trying on a black hat, whereas in the second version the hat is red. ... each participant will receive polarizing glasses that will block one of the two possible versions of the movie.

issues.description: The manuscript says pairs will be randomly assigned but gives no details on sequence generation, blocking, allocation concealment, or who implements assignment. These details are needed to assess bias and to replicate the study.
issues.quote: Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups

issues.description: Several interventions explicitly instruct participants to distrust external information and to answer from their own memory immediately before the final test. Any reduction in misinformation-consistent responses may therefore reflect a changed reporting criterion or compliance with demand characteristics rather than recovery or protection of memory. The design cannot distinguish these possibilities, yet the manuscript frames the effect as reducing memory conformity broadly.
issues.quote: The participants will be strongly encouraged to rely only on their own memory, not on any information stemming from the partner. ... Immediately after the participants are done with the methods of reducing memory conformity (or the control condition), they will complete the individual memory test

issues.description: The primary within-subject contrast compares discussed with non-discussed items. But discussed items differ from non-discussed items not only in exposure to discrepant information, but also in rehearsal, retrieval practice, and social discussion. Without a control condition involving discussion without discrepant information, the contrast conflates misinformation with generic discussion effects.
issues.quote: The correctness of answers to questions concerning discussed and non-discussed details will be compared.

issues.description: The Demonstration and motivation intervention assumes that most participants will experience a DRM false-memory illusion and therefore feel personally vulnerable. But the protocol provides no manipulation-check criterion for whether a participant actually showed the effect or how the intervention will be handled if they did not. The central mechanism of that condition is therefore not verified.
issues.quote: The DRM procedure usually results in most of the participants falsely recalling at least a few of the critical lures. ... The results will be fed back to participants in order to demonstrate to them that their memory was vulnerable to a subtle influence.

issues.description: The study uses deception and enrolls participants as young as 16, but the protocol does not report ethics approval, consent/assent procedures, parental consent for minors, or safeguards related to deception. These omissions are especially relevant in a study involving deliberate misleading cover stories and minors.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old ... We are interested in people’s sensory impressions at different levels of visual acuity.

issues.description: The sample is limited to young volunteers recruited via media/internet, yet the manuscript repeatedly motivates the work in terms of eyewitnesses and justice systems. Such a convenience sample may differ from real witnesses in age, stress, motivation, and context, so generalization to forensic settings is limited.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet.
